name: DBX
summary: Cross-platform database client for 100+ databases with desktop, Docker, CLI, built-in AI SQL assistant and an MCP server.
use_cases: generate SQL from a plain-language description
let AI coding agents query configured databases over MCP
preview Parquet, CSV or JSON files by drag and drop
features: connect to 100+ databases in one tool
AI SQL assistant generating and explaining queries
edit and export query results in data grid

pitfalls.readme_said: Download the latest release from the Releases page (Linux install shown only via Flatpak from FlatPark)
pitfalls.actually_needed: The AppImage DBX_0.6.71_amd64.AppImage from GitHub releases runs without root via --appimage-extract-and-run

pitfalls.readme_said: SQLite connection with a file path
pitfalls.actually_needed: The SQLite file must already exist; DBX reports 'file does not exist' and does not create a new one (op 9)
The file-export path could not be completed by the operator here (op 13); Copy as CSV to the clipboard worked

operations.feature: connect to 100+ databases in one tool
operations.goal: In DBX, create a new connection: choose SQLite (under Lightweight), name it pk{nonce}, and in the File Path field type the existing file /home/sbx/pickfit-data/test.db, then save. Open a new SQL query editor for that connection, type: SELECT SUM(qty)*100 AS total FROM items; and run it (Run button). Leave the results grid visible showing the computed value.
operations.observed: on screen (read by the screen judge, claude-opus-5-5, from pickfit's last screenshot): "57900": yes

operations.feature: edit and export query results in data grid
operations.goal: In DBX, create a new connection: choose SQLite (under Lightweight), name it pk{nonce}, File Path /home/sbx/pickfit-data/test.db, save. Open a new SQL query editor for that connection, type: SELECT name, qty*7 AS weekly FROM items; and click Run. In the results grid, select all result rows (click a cell then press Ctrl+A), then right-click a selected cell and choose the Copy as CSV option from the context menu (or use the results' Export menu's copy-to-clipboard option for CSV). The results must end up on the clipboard as CSV.
